turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because... I mean, I know elevators aren't actually dangerous. But whenever I have to get in one, I just get really scared, like I'm going to be trapped in there. I just can't seem to make myself feel normal about it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an intense fear of a specific situation (elevators) while acknowledging that the fear is out of proportion to the actual danger.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient states they get really scared 'whenever' they have to get in an elevator, indicating the situation consistently provokes an immediate fear response.
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient indicates that when they 'have to get in one', they endure the situation with intense fear and feel like they will be trapped.

turns.doctor_question: When you are in other situations, such as being in a crowded room or around people you don't know, do you feel that same sense of intense fear?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I work on construction sites, so I'm around a lot of different people all the time, and it doesn't bother me. It's really just the elevators. Crowds or strangers are totally fine.
